text:
alyssa: Heads-up — enterprise customer (CorpX) opened a P1: streaming responses from our /v1/generate endpoint are cutting off mid-event when they go through their gRPC gateway. Works if client hits our endpoint directly. They see partial SSE events and then the connection closes. Repro steps below.

ben: ack, can you paste the request + any logs? is this only HTTP/2 path?

alyssa: short repro:
1) client -> internal gRPC gateway (translates to HTTP/2 to our infra) -> our edge (HTTP/2) -> service (our runtime)
2) start a streaming generation (~20 tokens)
3) client receives a couple event chunks, then final event truncated, connection resets.

curl repro I gave them:
```bash
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=rwd-13b"
```
They also tried disabling HTTP/2 on the gateway and it works consistently (HTTP/1.1 passthrough).

diane: interesting. sounds like an intermediary is doing buffering/rewriting for HTTP/2 streams. any `Content-Length` / `Transfer-Encoding` differences in our edge logs?

alyssa: edge logs for that request id: `req=rx-0a1b2c3d` show status 200, streaming start, then `connection: reset by peer` after ~430ms. No explicit Content-Length on the response (SSE).

irina: two known patterns: proxies that convert to gRPC/HTTP2 may re-chunk or buffer until window fills or they see end-of-stream. also some grpc-gateway implementations buffer small responses and only flush on full frame boundary. cloud load balancers sometimes coalesce frames.

eng-oncall-bot: automated note: incident created INC-2026-045. Priority: P1. On-call: ben.

ben: on it; first hypothesis: gateway is converting SSE (text/event-stream) into a framed gRPC or HTTP/2 stream where intermediate buffering drops partial DATA frames. can we get a tcpdump from customer side showing RST or GOAWAY?

alyssa: customer attached a PCAP showing FIN from gateway when they abort; no GOAWAY from our side. They also included gateway logs with `grpc-status=13` on the gateway -> upstream call.

diane: grpc-status=13 == internal error. gateway probably treated the SSE as an HTTP response body that it wasn't expecting. Do we set `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and keep `Transfer-Encoding` off? For HTTP/2 there is no chunked transfer-encoding header; the proxy might inject or expect it incorrectly.

irina: ask customer for exact gateway vendor/version. Some older `grpc-gateway` proxies have a setting `--streaming-mode=buffer` vs `--streaming-mode=passthrough`. If it's buffering, small SSE events can be coalesced and then truncated on reconnect.

alyssa: they said "Envoy-based gateway v1.25" with a custom filter stack (transform filter).

ben: Envoy filter stacks are tricky — `envoy.filters.http.stream` or `buffer` filters can cause this. can you confirm headers from our response?

alyssa: headers at edge (exact):
```
:status: 200
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
cache-control: no-cache, no-transform
server: redwood-edge
x-request-id: rx-0a1b2c3d
```
No `content-length`, no `transfer-encoding` header (http2).

ben: ok. try two experiments: (A) have the runtime emit a larger SSE comment every N tokens so the intermediary has a bigger frame to forward (to see if it's a buffering window issue). (B) add `cache-control: no-transform` (already present) and `x-accel-buffering: no` (some proxies respect it). also add `connection: keep-alive` on H1 clients — but that won't affect h2.

diane: we should also expose a debug route that forces `Content-Length` by buffering the entire response (bad perf) — useful to prove buffering is the cause.

alyssa: customer ran experiment A. When runtime emitted a 1KB keepalive comment every 100ms the stream stayed alive and complete. When small events only, it truncated.

irina: that strongly suggests the gateway is buffering until some frame size/time then giving up. What does Envoy do with HTTP/1.1 upstream vs HTTP/2? If the gateway speaks h2 to upstream and uses a transform filter, it may reconstruct frames badly.

ben: next steps for us:
- try reproducing in our staging Envoy with the same filter config.
- add an optional response header `x-rwd-debug-stream: passthrough` that we can ask the customer to trust to see if their gateway disables buffers for that header.
- create a minimal Node/Go client to test h2c vs h1.

diane: put a reproducible test into `eng-infra` staging: a tiny SSE server that emits 5 small events and then ends. run through an Envoy config that matches their transform filter.

alyssa: customer approved us to hit their gateway with a test client. asking for ETA.

ben: I've slotted a reproducer job now. Quick hack: try setting `connection: upgrade`? probably not applicable. Also try `trailer: x-stream-end`? h2 trailers are allowed but intermediaries sometimes choke.

irina: other mitigation: have client force HTTP/1.1 to our edge (they already did that and it worked). For longer-term: document that some gRPC gateways should use passthrough streaming or not apply rewrite filters to `text/event-stream`. Add a compatibility note in support KB.

alyssa: customer is asking for timeline. Can we give quick mitigation: 1) set gateway to pass streaming responses unbuffered, 2) client fallback to HTTP/1.1, or 3) add keepalive padding as a workaround.

ben: yes. I'll draft a KB note and the infra reproducer. If the gateway team shares their filter config we can point to exact envoys flags (e.g., `streaming_mode: passthrough` in their filter).

support-bot: @alyssa FYI added KB draft ticket KB-2026-117 and linked INC-2026-045.

diane: one more gotcha: some proxies translate chunk boundaries into separate DATA frames and then reassemble differently. On our side ensure we flush after every SSE event: runtime should call `flush()` on the response writer immediately after writing the event and before writing the next. For our go runtime that means `w.(http.Flusher).Flush()`.

alyssa: noted. I asked runtime team to add an opt-in flush toggle behind a config flag so we can enable and test with customer quickly.

ben: I'll follow up with a staging repro + patch for the KB today. If we can reproduce with Envoy we can tag the exact filter setting.

alyssa: thanks team. I'll keep customer updated and post gateway config when they send it. :thumbsup:
